messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: synth-check 'prod-canary-eu' failed 3x within 2m — threshold breach, firing page to on-call.

pagerduty: PagerDuty — Incident INC-20260314-72 created, page routed to jordan (sre on-call). Link: https://pd.example/INC-20260314-72

jordan: on it, acked the page. I'll gather initial scope. What regions impacted?

maria: I'm seeing the same probe failures from eu-west-1 and eu-central. All checks timeout around 1.2s then 504 from the canary frontend. No upstream model errors yet.

lee: logs look like repeated TLS handshake resets to the canary workers. snippet:
```
2026-03-14T13:10:05Z canary-runner-3 tls: handshake error: EOF
2026-03-14T13:10:06Z canary-runner-3 http: 504 gateway timeout
``` 

jordan: good capture — any recent deploys to canary runtime in EU?

maria: no code deploys. Infra autoscaler did a small surge earlier (burst to handle load) then an ATO event from the cloud provider changed ephemeral IPs.

ops-bot: Noted cloud provider maintenance in eu-west-1 between 13:00-13:30 UTC. Posterior events might be related.

lee: hypothesis: the canary runner pods lose established connections during node NIC reassign; KV cache warmups fail -> timeouts. Suggest: 1) spin up fresh canary-runner replicas on unaffected AZ, 2) route synthetic checks to secondary region while we mitigate.

jordan: action plan: (a) scale canary-runner up to 6 replicas in EU, (b) add a routing override to route synth checks to staging-eu for next 15m, (c) notify customers if service-level probes degrade > 30m.

jordan: running scale command now:
```
kubectl -n synthetic scale deploy/canary-runner --replicas=6
``` 

maria: scaling triggered, new pods pending on eu-central-azb.

lee: I pushed a routing override to the synth proxy: /synth -> staging-eu for team-canary. Config snippet:
```
routeOverride:
  match: /synth
  destination: staging-eu
  ttl: 900
```

jordan: route change applied. Monitoring latency and success rates. Can everyone watch for decreases in probe failures?

ops-bot: synth proxy routing change committed by lee (rollout id rlt-5589). ETA 20s.

maria: failures dropping — current failure rate eu-west ~8% -> 0.9% in the last 2m. Good.

pagerduty: jordan acknowledged the incident at 2026-03-14T13:12:11Z.

jordan: I want to avoid noisy pages — lowering threshold for EU synthetic alerts (increase consecutive failures threshold from 3 -> 5) while the cloud maintenance window completes. I'll revert once stable.

lee: lowered threshold in synth-monitor config and reloaded:
```
consecutive_failures: 5
rollout: synth-monitor/roll-191
```

maria: customer impact: internal telemetry shows 0.4% of production inference requests experienced elevated tail latency around the window, no errors surfaced to end-users via product metrics. I've opened a quick post-incident note in ops-runbook.

eng-oncall: ping — if latency resurfaces after maintenance we'll consider a full canary job restart and node drain of impacted hosts.

jordan: agree. For now: 1) close immediate page, 2) continue to monitor for 30m, 3) start next on-call handoff with context if escalation needed.

jordan: resolving page in PagerDuty (ack -> resolve) since failure rate is back within temporary mitigation.

pagerduty: Incident INC-20260314-72 resolved by jordan at 2026-03-14T13:18:03Z. Notes: routing override applied; scaled canary-runner; threshold adjusted during cloud maintenance.

jordan: handoff notes for next on-call (cc @eng-oncall):
- root cause hypothesis: cloud NIC/ephemeral IP churn during provider maintenance caused TLS resets to canary-runner.
- mitigations applied: scaled canary-runner, routing override to staging-eu, monitor threshold adjusted.
- next steps: consider pod anti-affinity to spread canary runners across stable hosts; confirm with cloud support whether maintenance may re-run.

maria: adding links: logs collected -> s3://redwood-ops/logs/INC-20260314-72/, probe graphs -> https://metrics.redwood/synth/INC-20260314-72

lee: putting a follow-up ticket for infra: INFRA-879 to evaluate canary pod affinity and NIC resilience.

jordan: thanks everyone. I'll re-open or escalate if we see regressions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed after 35 minutes of inactivity. If anomalies recur, a new page will be fired.
